key_insight: Physical photonic noise can behave like a built-in regularizer in hybrid quantum neural networks, but its benefit depends strongly on the dataset.
engineering_relevance: Instead of always suppressing hardware noise, photonic QNN designers may be able to tune it as a free training-time regularizer for better generalization on some tasks.
method: Built PHQCNNs in Quandela Perceval with the MerLin framework.
Injected a 7-parameter physical noise model directly during training.
Used a genetic algorithm to search noise settings and compared them against a noiseless baseline across five seeds.
evidence_signal: GA-tuned noise improved validation accuracy on Iris by +0.82 percentage points and Digits by +1.45 points, but reduced MNIST accuracy by -1.21 points.
watch_item: The regularization effect is not universal, so noise tuning may help some datasets while harming others and should be validated case by case.
paper_title: PN-QNN: Harnessing Physical Noise as a Native Regularizer in Photonic Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks
